correctness.rationale: Both factored reconstructions reduce to scalar all-ones matrices because biregularity makes every row sum and every column sum equal. The first raw-update RMS is exactly \((1-\beta_2^t)^{-1/2}\), so source clipping at threshold one removes the entire first-stage transient. The momentum and confidence states then have closed scalar recurrences. Direct replay of the embedded verifier matches every formula.

value.rationale: Confidence normalization is CAME's defining addition to Adafactor. The theorem identifies an exact boundary behavior of that mechanism: perfectly consistent updates make confidence increase until it is limited only by the explicit epsilon floor, while biregular sparsity remains invisible to global RMS and receives an exact inverse-square-root active-coordinate gain. This directly clarifies what the confidence statistic controls and what it cannot distinguish.
